name: qwen-ast-patch — Local Method Patcher
description: Decomposed-generation webhook: calls local qwen2.5-coder:7b (Ollama) for a single method, then patches it into an existing Ruby file via AST-located insert/replace (ast_patch_ruby.rb) instead of full-file rewrite — companion to hybrid-dev-loop's step 1b.

parameters.jsCode:
// Échappement shell : une valeur venant de la requête ne doit jamais sortir de ses apostrophes
function shq(s) { return "'" + String(s).replace(/'/g, "'\''") + "'"; }
var AST_PATCH_SRC = "#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# ast_patch_ruby.rb — insert or replace a single method in an existing Ruby
# file without touching anything else in it.
#
# Design: locate-and-splice, never parse-and-reprint. Parser::Source::Rewriter
# only replaces/inserts text at the exact byte ranges of the AST nodes it
# touches — every other line (formatting, comments, unrelated methods) stays
# byte-for-byte identical. A full parse->AST->reprint round trip was avoided
# on purpose: Ruby's grammar loses/reflows comments and whitespace on
# reprint, which would defeat the whole point of this tool (guaranteeing
# sibling methods are never disturbed).
#
# Usage:
#   ruby ast_patch_ruby.rb --file app/services/foo_service.rb --method call \
#     --body /tmp/new_call_method.rb [--insert-after other_method] \
#     [--visibility public|private|protected] [--write]
#
# --visibility (insert): place the new method at the end of that section of the
# class — before the first bare `private`/`protected` for public, after the
# last method of the matching bare section otherwise, creating
# `private`/`protected` at the end of the class when the section doesn't exist.
# Without it, the method is appended after the last method (old behaviour), so
# it silently inherits the visibility of whatever section comes last. With
# --insert-after, the anchor decides; a --visibility that disagrees with the
# anchor's section is an error. On replace the method keeps its place; a
# --visibility that disagrees with its current one is an error.
# The resulting visibility is always reported in the JSON output.
#
# stdin body: pass --body - to read the new method source from stdin instead
# of a file.
#
# Output (stdout, JSON, always — this is the machine-readable contract the
# n8n workflow parses):
#   success: {"ok":true,"action":"replaced"|"inserted","method":"name","visibility":"public"|"private"|"protected","content":"<full patched file>"}
#   failure: {"ok":false,"error":"..."}
# Exit code 0 on success, 1 on usage/lookup error, 2 on a patch that would
# produce invalid Ruby (caught before anything is written).

require 'parser/current'
require 'optparse'
require 'json'

options = { write: false }
OptionParser.new do |opts|
  opts.on('--file PATH') { |v| options[:file] = v }
  opts.on('--method NAME') { |v| options[:method] = v }
  opts.on('--body PATH') { |v| options[:body] = v }
  opts.on('--insert-after NAME') { |v| options[:insert_after] = v }
  opts.on('--in-class NAME') { |v| options[:in_class] = v }
  opts.on('--ruby-version VERSION') { |v| options[:ruby_version] = v }
  opts.on('--visibility VIS') { |v| options[:visibility] = v }
  opts.on('--write') { options[:write] = true }
end.parse!

def fail_json(message, code: 1)
  puts JSON.generate({ ok: false, error: message })
  exit(code)
end

%i[file method body].each do |req|
  fail_json("missing required option --#{req.to_s.tr('_', '-')}") unless options[req]
end

fail_json("file not found: #{options[:file]}") unless File.exist?(options[:file])
VISIBILITIES = %w[public private protected].freeze
if options[:visibility] && !VISIBILITIES.include?(options[:visibility])
  fail_json("--visibility must be one of #{VISIBILITIES.join(', ')} (got #{options[:visibility].inspect})")
end

body_source =
  if options[:body] == '-'
    $stdin.read
  else
    fail_json("body file not found: #{options[:body]}") unless File.exist?(options[:body])
    File.read(options[:body])
  end
body_source = body_source.strip
fail_json('body is empty') if body_source.empty?
unless body_source.start_with?('def ')
  fail_json("body must be a single method starting with 'def ' (got: #{body_source[0, 30].inspect}...)")
end

RUBY_PARSER_BY_VERSION = {
  '3.0' => 'Parser::Ruby30', '3.1' => 'Parser::Ruby31',
  '3.2' => 'Parser::Ruby32', '3.3' => 'Parser::Ruby33'
}.freeze

parser_class =
  if options[:ruby_version]
    const_name = RUBY_PARSER_BY_VERSION[options[:ruby_version]]
    fail_json("unsupported --ruby-version #{options[:ruby_version]}") unless const_name
    Object.const_get(const_name)
  else
    Parser::CurrentRuby
  end

source = File.read(options[:file])
buffer = Parser::Source::Buffer.new(options[:file], source: source)

begin
  ast = parser_class.new.tap { |p| p.diagnostics.all_errors_are_fatal = true }.parse(buffer)
rescue Parser::SyntaxError => e
  fail_json("could not parse #{options[:file]}: #{e.message}")
end
fail_json("#{options[:file]} is empty or has no parseable content") if ast.nil?

# --- find the innermost class/module node (descend through module wrappers) ---
def find_container(node, wanted_name)
  return nil unless node.is_a?(Parser::AST::Node)

  if %i[class module].include?(node.type)
    name = node.children.first
    const_name = name&.children&.last
    if wanted_name.nil? || const_name.to_s == wanted_name
      body = node.children.last
      # descend further only if the whole body is a single nested class/module
      if body && %i[class module].include?(body.type)
        nested = find_container(body, wanted_name)
        return nested if nested
      end
      return node if node.type == :class
    end
  end

  node.children.each do |child|
    found = find_container(child, wanted_name)
    return found if found
  end
  nil
end

container = find_container(ast, options[:in_class])
fail_json('no class definition found in file (module-only or script-level files are not supported yet)') unless container

# --- collect def/defs nodes matching the target method name, anywhere under the container ---
def find_defs(node, method_name, acc = [])
  return acc unless node.is_a?(Parser::AST::Node)

  if (node.type == :def && node.children[0] == method_name.to_sym) ||
     (node.type == :defs && node.children[1] == method_name.to_sym)
    acc << node
  end
  node.children.each { |c| find_defs(c, method_name, acc) }
  acc
end

matches = find_defs(container, options[:method])
if matches.size > 1
  fail_json("method '#{options[:method]}' is ambiguous (#{matches.size} definitions found) — " \
            'narrow with --in-class, or this file needs a more specific target')
end

rewriter = Parser::Source::TreeRewriter.new(buffer)
indent = ' ' * (container.loc.keyword.column + 2)

# skip_first: true when the replacement text lands exactly at an existing
# node's start column (a `replace`) — that column's whitespace is already in
# the untouched source before the range, so re-adding it would double it up.
# false for a fresh `insert`, where no whitespace precedes the new text yet.
# Prefixes every line with `indent` while preserving each line's own
# relative whitespace (so nested body/end lines stay nested under `def`) —
# except line 0 when skip_first, which already sits at the right column via
# untouched source text before it (a `replace`, not an `insert`).
def reindent(src, indent, skip_first:)
  lines = src.split("\n")
  lines.each_with_index.map do |l, i|
    next l if skip_first && i.zero?
    l.strip.empty? ? '' : "#{indent}#{l}"
  end.join("\n")
end

# Default anchor when --insert-after isn't given: the last def/defs directly
# in the class body (i.e. append after the last existing method) — this
# reuses the exact same insert_after mechanics as an explicit anchor instead
# of computing new whitespace math against container.loc.end, which is
# fiddly to get right (the indentation already sitting right before that
# token belongs to the closing `end`, not to freshly inserted content).
def last_direct_method(container)
  body = container.children.last
  direct =
    case body&.type
    when :begin then body.children.select { |c| c.is_a?(Parser::AST::Node) && %i[def defs].include?(c.type) }
    when :def, :defs then [body]
    else []
    end
  direct.last
end

# --- visibility sections of the class body --------------------------------
# Walks the direct statements in order, like Ruby does: a bare `private` /
# `protected` / `public` changes the default for the defs that follow;
# `private def x` and `private :x` only affect that method.
MODIFIERS = %i[public private protected].freeze

def body_statements(container)
  body = container.children.last
  return [] unless body

  body.type == :begin ? body.children.select { |c| c.is_a?(Parser::AST::Node) } : [body]
end

def bare_modifier(stmt)
  stmt.type == :send && stmt.children[0].nil? && MODIFIERS.include?(stmt.children[1]) && stmt.children.size == 2
end

# [{node:, name:, vis:, inline:, index:}] for every instance method directly in the body,
# plus [{node:, vis:, index:}] for the bare modifiers.
def scan_visibility(stmts)
  state = :public
  defs, modifiers, explicit = [], [], {}
  stmts.each_with_index do |stmt, i|
    if bare_modifier(stmt)
      state = stmt.children[1]
      modifiers << { node: stmt, vis: state, index: i }
    elsif stmt.type == :send && stmt.children[0].nil? && MODIFIERS.include?(stmt.children[1])
      stmt.children[2..].each do |arg|
        if arg.type == :def
          defs << { node: arg, name: arg.children[0], vis: stmt.children[1], inline: true, index: i }
        elsif %i[sym str].include?(arg.type)
          explicit[arg.children[0].to_sym] = stmt.children[1]
        end
      end
    elsif stmt.type == :def
      defs << { node: stmt, name: stmt.children[0], vis: state, inline: false, index: i }
    end
  end
  defs.each { |d| d[:vis] = explicit[d[:name]] if explicit.key?(d[:name]) }
  [defs, modifiers]
end

stmts = body_statements(container)
defs, modifiers = scan_visibility(stmts)
wanted_vis = options[:visibility]&.to_sym

action =
  if matches.empty? && wanted_vis && !options[:insert_after] && !stmts.empty?
    new_method_text = reindent(body_source, indent, skip_first: false)
    if wanted_vis == :public
      first_mod = modifiers.find { |m| m[:vis] != :public }
      publics = defs.select { |d| d[:vis] == :public && !d[:inline] && (first_mod.nil? || d[:index] < first_mod[:index]) }
      if publics.any?
        rewriter.insert_after(publics.last[:node].loc.expression, "\n\n#{new_method_text}")
      elsif first_mod
        # no public method yet: goes right before the first `private`/`protected`
        rewriter.insert_before(first_mod[:node].loc.expression,
                               "#{reindent(body_source, indent, skip_first: true)}\n\n#{indent}")
      else
        rewriter.insert_after(stmts.last.loc.expression, "\n\n#{new_method_text}")
      end
    else
      section = modifiers.select { |m| m[:vis] == wanted_vis }.last
      if section
        next_mod = modifiers.find { |m| m[:index] > section[:index] }
        in_section = defs.select { |d| d[:index] > section[:index] && (next_mod.nil? || d[:index] < next_mod[:index]) && !d[:inline] }
        anchor = in_section.last&.dig(:node) || section[:node]
        rewriter.insert_after(anchor.loc.expression, "\n\n#{new_method_text}")
      else
        # no such section yet: open it at the end of the class
        rewriter.insert_after(stmts.last.loc.expression, "\n\n#{indent}#{wanted_vis}\n\n#{new_method_text}")
      end
    end
    'inserted'
  elsif matches.empty?
    new_method_text = reindent(body_source, indent, skip_first: false)
    anchor =
      if options[:insert_after]
        found = find_defs(container, options[:insert_after]).first
        fail_json("--insert-after target '#{options[:insert_after]}' not found") unless found
        found
      else
        last_direct_method(container)
      end

    if anchor
      rewriter.insert_after(anchor.loc.expression, "\n\n#{new_method_text}")
    else
      # empty class body — nothing to anchor after
      rewriter.insert_before(container.loc.end, "\n#{new_method_text}\n#{' ' * container.loc.keyword.column}")
    end
    'inserted'
  else
    current = defs.find { |d| d[:node].equal?(matches.first) }
    if wanted_vis && current && current[:vis] != wanted_vis
      fail_json("'#{options[:method]}' is currently #{current[:vis]}; replace keeps a method in place — " \
                "move it by hand if its visibility must change")
    end
    new_method_text = reindent(body_source, indent, skip_first: true)
    rewriter.replace(matches.first.loc.expression, new_method_text)
    'replaced'
  end

patched = rewriter.process

# safety net: never hand back something that doesn't parse
begin
  parser_class.new.tap { |p| p.diagnostics.all_errors_are_fatal = true }
              .parse(Parser::Source::Buffer.new(options[:file], source: patched))
rescue Parser::SyntaxError => e
  fail_json("patch produced invalid Ruby, nothing written: #{e.message}", code: 2)
end

# resulting visibility, read back from the patched file (the only reliable source)
patched_ast = parser_class.new.parse(Parser::Source::Buffer.new(options[:file], source: patched))
patched_defs, = scan_visibility(body_statements(find_container(patched_ast, options[:in_class])))
result_vis = patched_defs.find { |d| d[:name] == options[:method].to_sym }&.dig(:vis)
if options[:insert_after] && wanted_vis && result_vis && result_vis != wanted_vis
  fail_json("--insert-after '#{options[:insert_after]}' is in the #{result_vis} section but --visibility is " \
            "#{wanted_vis}: omit --insert-after to let the section decide")
end

File.write(options[:file], patched) if options[:write]

puts JSON.generate({ ok: true, action: action, method: options[:method], visibility: result_vis, content: patched })
";
var methodBody = $json.methodBody;
var targetFile = $('Normalize Input').first().json.targetFile;
var method = $('Normalize Input').first().json.method;
var insertAfter = $('Normalize Input').first().json.insertAfter;
var visibility = $('Normalize Input').first().json.visibility;
var container = $('Normalize Input').first().json.container;
var scriptB64 = Buffer.from(AST_PATCH_SRC).toString('base64');
var bodyB64 = Buffer.from(methodBody).toString('base64');
var insertAfterArg = insertAfter ? (" --insert-after " + shq(insertAfter)) : '';
// public|private|protected only (validated in Normalize Input), safe to inline in the shell command
var visibilityArg = visibility ? (" --visibility " + visibility) : '';
var sh = "mkdir -p tmp/ast_patch && echo '" + scriptB64 + "' | base64 -d > tmp/ast_patch/ast_patch_ruby.rb && echo '" + bodyB64 + "' | base64 -d > tmp/ast_patch/new_method.rb && ruby tmp/ast_patch/ast_patch_ruby.rb --file " + shq(targetFile) + " --method " + shq(method) + insertAfterArg + visibilityArg + " --body tmp/ast_patch/new_method.rb --write";
return [{ json: {
  container: container,
  targetFile: targetFile,
  method: method,
  dockerBridgePayload: { container: container, args: ['sh', '-c', sh] }
} }];
